$comment: How the plugin talks to Scenario's REST API (docs/spec/SPEC.md sections 2.3, 3.13 and 4). Data, not code, so a change on Scenario's side needs no code change. The Authorization header goes to base_url only. Measured live on 2026-10-19 with an Editor Project key unless a comment says otherwise.

sign_in.$comment: Save and test and Test connection run two free reads. auth_check needs a valid key (private models). projects returns the key's project with its name, id and keys; the plugin finds its own key by apiKeyId and keeps only the project name, the project id and its own role and scope. The same answer lists members' emails and every key id: it is never logged, stored or sent to the helper.

roles_that_cannot_generate.$comment: Inferred from Scenario's description of the Reader role (read-only); a Reader key's dry run was not measured. Custom roles are not judged.

known_errors.$comment: Error bodies carry `reason` (400, 403, 404) or `message` (401, 413), never a code. A known text (matched without case, as a substring) at its status gives an error type of shared/errors.json; any other answer is classified by status and shows Scenario's text. An unknown key answers 403, not 401.

links.$comment: Opened in the browser after Photoshop asks the person. Scenario documents no deep link to the API keys page (Settings > Organization > API Keys), so create_key opens the help center article that explains it.
